summary: AUDIT LOG HARDENING (Enterprise Grade) - Completed comprehensive testing. Fixed critical bug where AuditLog response model was missing required fields (ip_address, user_role, timestamp) and had non-optional object_id causing 500 errors. All 16 audit logging tests now pass.

resolved.issue: AuditLog response model missing ip_address, user_role, timestamp fields
resolved.resolution: Added new fields to AuditLog model: user_id, user_name, user_role, entity_type, entity_id, ip_address, timestamp

resolved.issue: object_id field was non-optional (str) but LOGIN_FAILED logs have null entity_id
resolved.resolution: Changed object_id to Optional[str] in AuditLog model

resolved.issue: Audit logs endpoint not properly mapping legacy vs new fields
resolved.resolution: Added field mapping logic in list_audit_logs endpoint

context_for_next_testing_agent: Audit logging enterprise-grade implementation verified. All critical actions logged to audit_logs collection with required fields: user_id, user_role, action, entity_type, entity_id, old_value, new_value, timestamp, ip_address. The audit_service.py uses try/catch safety wrappers so audit failures don't break main endpoints. IP addresses captured from X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP headers, or request.client.host.
